reason: Forcing the self-skip guard true makes computeSeparation continue on every neighbor and always return {0,0}, an observable force change no test currently pins.
Changing overlap + 1 to overlap - 1 flips the sign of the separation strength when overlap is 0, an observable force difference.
Forcing the targetId guard false stops skipping the target neighbor, so a separation force is wrongly applied toward the target.
Setting the coincident-body nudge distance to 2 instead of 1 changes the computed separation force magnitude, observable via computeSeparation.
Flipping === to !== inverts which neighbor is treated as the target, changing which neighbors contribute to the force.
The mutated bounds.height*2 only enlarges and shifts the tree's boundary half-height; every body still lies inside it and query results depend on point positions, so no query output changes.
Forcing the !bounds guard false lets a null bounds through to new Rectangle, throwing on empty body maps; a build-with-no-bodies test would catch it.
Forcing the fixed-world-bounds guard true skips body-based bounds computation even for null or sub-minWorldSize world bounds, changing the resulting tree.
avoidanceForce*0.5 to /0.5 changes the avoidance scale, but the only test uses spatialIndex null so the avoidanceMagnitude>0 block is never exercised.
avoidanceX*avoidanceScale to /avoidanceScale changes the applied avoidance acceleration, uncaught because the sole test never enters the avoidance branch.
Forcing the degenerate guard false makes getVelocityProxy return {vx,vy} for non-finite or sub-epsilon velocities instead of {0,0}, an observable difference for a NaN-velocity body.
vy/len to vy*len denormalizes the heading y-component returned by getHeading, changing obstacle-avoidance direction.
Changing the fallback mass from 1 to 2 halves the seek force whenever body.mass is non-finite or non-positive, observable via computeSeek.
Returning undefined instead of {0,0} for a static body breaks computeSeek's contract and makes applySeek throw on force.x.
<= to < changes behavior exactly when len equals MIN_DISTANCE, where the mutant computes a seek force instead of returning {0,0}; no boundary test covers this.
Forcing safeDt<=0 guard true makes stepVerlet always zero acceleration and skip integration, freezing motion for any positive dt.
Math.random()*20 to /20 only changes random radii for benchmark body setup, which carries no assertions and never runs under the graded test suite.
The mutated this.x - this.width is inside Rectangle.intersects (the allocating variant), which is never called anywhere; the hot path uses intersectsRaw.
Forcing the this.sw guard false skips Quadtree.release on the sw subtree in clear(), a side-effect on pool state a test could assert.
> to >= in intersectsRaw changes inclusion exactly when the query box edge touches the boundary edge; no test places a point exactly on the edge.

width/2 to width*2 only enlarges child boundaries; queryRaw filters by point position and any child containing a matched point still intersects the query box, so every query returns identical results and recursion stays bounded.
Defaulting invalidationMuted to true suppresses the mutation-summary publish in addEntity on a fresh (un-hydrated) runtime, an observable invalidation-event difference.
Returning undefined instead of this.state.tick changes the observable return value of the public stepOncePreservingPause().
=== to !== leaves a zero timeScale unfixed (division by zero for dt) while rewriting every nonzero scale to 1, an observable behavior change.
Forcing the non-fatal guard false makes pause() a no-op that never sets status to paused, an observable state difference.
Returning undefined instead of 1 from the sort comparator's empty-id branch changes ordering of entities with empty ids; no test mixes an empty-id entity.
Forcing the !body guard false indexes undefined bodies into physicsIndex, so getPhysicsBody returns undefined entries instead of none; no test covers entities lacking a physics body.
Returning undefined instead of 0 for a missing sys_world in getGlobal changes the observable return; the engine suite runs but never asserts getGlobal's value.
Returning undefined instead of the entry value / 0 changes getGlobal's observable return, which the engine suite executes but does not assert.
